meta.source: English - CUET Pro (4).html: CHAPTERS, CHAPTER_INSIGHTS, SUBDESC, ENG_ORDER
meta.notes: chapters.<id>.notes.<topicId> are HTML strings (use a sanitizer). Word-bank data is in cuetpro_english_word_banks.json. pyqBank here covers ALL topics (reading comprehension, vocabulary, grammar). answer is a 0-based option index.

tips.title: Factual passages are the bulk
tips.detail: Roughly 10 of every ~13 RC questions come from factual / expository prose — practise skimming argument structure, not literary appreciation.

tips.title: Read the question before the passage
tips.detail: Most RC questions are direct-retrieval (Easy/Medium). Knowing what you're hunting for saves the most time.

tips.title: Don't over-invest in poetry
tips.detail: Literary + poem passages together are only about 1 question per paper — know the common figures of speech and move on.

tips.title: A vocabulary line hides in every passage
tips.detail: A synonym / 'the word X in the passage means' question is almost always one of the 5 — treat it as a Vocabulary mark, not an RC one.

difficult.title: Inference & tone in factual passages
difficult.why: The distractors are all 'partly true' — these are where accuracy drops under time pressure.

difficult.title: Poetry — 'what the poet means' lines
difficult.why: Figurative language and compressed syntax make the literal answer hard to pin down quickly.

difficult.title: Long argumentative passages
difficult.why: Five questions on a dense 400-word passage is the biggest single time sink in the paper.

tips.title: This is where the paper is won
tips.detail: Vocabulary is ~53% of every paper — more than Reading Comprehension and Grammar combined.

tips.title: Drill the big four
tips.detail: Word Usage, Rearranging the Parts, Synonyms and Antonyms are ~4–6 questions each, every paper.

tips.title: Para-jumbles need a method, not speed
tips.detail: Almost always tagged Medium: find the opening sentence, then follow pronoun and linker chains.

tips.title: Idioms & phrasal verbs reward rote
tips.detail: Build a deck and revise it — close-meaning distractors are the only real trap.

tips.title: Spelling & foreign words are free marks
tips.detail: Under 1 question per paper each, but pure recall — a single revision pass is enough.

difficult.title: Rearranging the Parts (para-jumbles)
difficult.why: Highest volume in the section and easy to lose 2–3 marks on when rushed.

difficult.title: Idioms with near-synonym options
difficult.why: Two options often both look plausible unless you know the exact idiom.

difficult.title: Analogies
difficult.why: Spotting the precise relationship type (part-whole, cause-effect, degree) is the whole question.

tips.title: Don't over-prepare the rare topics
tips.detail: Grammar is ~1 question in 6, split across 16 areas — Subject–Verb Agreement, Conditionals and Pronouns barely appear.

tips.title: Focus the big six
tips.detail: Prepositions, Tenses, Voice, Speech, Error Detection and Modals carry most grammar marks.

tips.title: Voice & Speech are pure rule-following
tips.detail: Active↔passive and direct↔indirect transformations follow fixed steps — reliable marks once drilled.

tips.title: Preposition questions have no shortcut
tips.detail: They test collocation (invested in, affinity with) — exposure and a phrasal-preposition list beat rules here.

difficult.title: Preposition collocations
difficult.why: No governing rule — each is memorised usage, and the four options are often all grammatical in isolation.

difficult.title: Error Detection across a 4-part sentence
difficult.why: You have to find which segment is wrong and why, under one-mark time budget.

difficult.title: Tense sequence in multi-blank sentences
difficult.why: 'By the time X, Y had…' pairs need the whole timeline right, not just one verb.

subdesc.rc-literary: Poems and literary prose extracts — mostly 'what the line means' and 'which device'.
subdesc.rc-factual: Expository / argumentative passages — direct-retrieval, main idea, inference, tone.
subdesc.rc-narrative: First-person accounts or story extracts — sequence, character, the point of the story.
subdesc.vocab-analogies: A : B :: C : ? — identify and match the exact relationship between the pair.
subdesc.vocab-antonyms: Word most opposite in meaning; a near-synonym is planted as the decoy.
subdesc.vocab-synonyms: Word closest in meaning, sometimes in a sentence that fixes the shade wanted.
subdesc.vocab-idioms: Meaning or completion of a fixed phrase; the literal reading is always a distractor.
subdesc.vocab-word-usage: Fill-the-blank and 'used correctly/incorrectly' — collocation, register, confusable pairs.
subdesc.vocab-spelling: Pick the correctly / incorrectly spelt word from a small recurring pool.
subdesc.vocab-foreign-words: Meaning of borrowed expressions (bona fide, status quo, de facto…).
subdesc.vocab-phrasal-verbs: Verb + particle meaning, or the right particle to complete a sentence.
subdesc.vocab-rearranging: Para-jumbles — order 4–5 fragments into one coherent sentence.
subdesc.gr-sva: The verb must agree with its real subject; words in between don't change the number.
subdesc.gr-tenses: Correct verb form for a blank, usually with two events at different times.
subdesc.gr-articles: a / an / the / no article — first mention vs specific vs unique; sound not spelling.
subdesc.gr-prepositions: Right preposition in a fixed collocation (invest in, indistinguishable from…).
subdesc.gr-pronouns: Agreement and case — 'between you and me', reflexive only when subject = object.
subdesc.gr-adj-adv: Adjective vs adverb, and comparative / superlative forms.
subdesc.gr-conjunctions: Contrast / reason / condition / time linkers, and correlative pairs.
subdesc.gr-modals: can / could / must / should / need — the shade of meaning and the past form.
subdesc.gr-voice: Active ↔ passive: object → subject + be + past participle.
subdesc.gr-speech: Direct ↔ indirect — reporting verb, tense backshift, pronoun and time-word changes.
subdesc.gr-error-detection: Sentence in parts; find the one part with a grammatical error (or 'no error').
subdesc.gr-sentence-correction: Choose the one grammatically correct version out of four.
subdesc.gr-conditionals: Match the two halves of an 'if' sentence (types 0–3).
subdesc.gr-question-tags: The short tag added to a statement — positive statement → negative tag.
subdesc.gr-parts-of-speech: A word's part of speech in context, plus assertive ↔ exclamatory transforms.
subdesc.gr-literary-devices: Identify the figure of speech in a line — simile, metaphor, personification…

reading-comprehension.title: Reading Comprehension
reading-comprehension.desc: Passages and poems — the biggest single block of the paper after Vocabulary. Mostly direct-retrieval questions on factual and narrative prose, with a smaller share of literary and poetry passages.

vocabulary.title: Vocabulary
vocabulary.desc: Over half of every CUET English paper. Word usage, para-jumbles, synonyms and antonyms carry most of it; idioms, phrasal verbs, analogies, spelling and foreign words fill the rest.

grammar.title: Grammar
grammar.desc: Only about one question in six, spread thin across sixteen areas. Prepositions, tenses, voice, speech, error detection and modals do most of the work; the rest appear rarely.
